standard.title: Online text navigation features
standard.description: identify text navigation features of online texts that enhance readability including headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify the purpose of layout and navigation features in print and digital texts (AC9E3LA05). They have not yet examined the specific navigation features of online texts — headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout — as readability-enhancing choices.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify and explain the purpose of online text navigation features including headlines, drop-down menus, hyperlinks, graphics and layout, and describe how these features help readers select and navigate content purposefully.

nodes.label: Print vs online navigation features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare how print and online texts use different navigation features and explain what each type of feature does for the reader.
nodes.minimum_width: Name two navigation features specific to online texts (e.g. links, drop-down menus) and explain how each helps a reader.
nodes.typical_width: Compare navigation features in a print text (headings, subheadings, table of contents) with their online equivalents (home pages, subpages, hyperlinks, drop-down menus) and explain how online features extend or replace print conventions.
wider: Compare navigation features across two different websites on similar topics (e.g. two science information sites for students) and evaluate which is more readable and why
Design a navigation structure for a hypothetical webpage on a familiar topic and explain the purpose of each feature chosen
success_criteria: Can name at least two online-specific navigation features and explain their readability function
Can identify at least one way online navigation differs from print navigation

nodes.label: Headlines, graphics and layout
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how headlines, graphics and layout work together in online texts to guide reader selection and comprehension.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a headline, a graphic and a layout feature in an online text and explain what each contributes to readability.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how headlines, graphics and layout in an online text work together to signal what is important, guide navigation and support comprehension — including how graphics and captions add meaning beyond the body text.
wider: Compare how headlines and layout differ across online news sites for different audiences (children vs adults) and explain the design choices
Examine how the same story is presented with different headlines and layouts across two sites and discuss how design affects meaning
success_criteria: Can explain how a specific headline helps a reader decide whether to read further
Can explain how a graphic adds to rather than just repeats the text
